Subject: Third-party subprocessors & telemetry (post-call follow-up)

Hi John / Sara,

Great to meet on the call earlier — thanks for walking through Acme's use case and security checklist. Per our discussion, I wanted to recap the key items we committed to follow up on related to data handling, telemetry, and third-party subprocessors so you have everything in one place.

Recap / answers in brief:
- PII: Redwood does not index or persist customer prompt content as searchable metadata. Customer content is processed for inference; by default we do not use customer data for training.
- Data retention: Default request/trace logs are retained for 30 days; longer retention can be configured for Dedicated/Private deployments per contract.
- Logging controls: We can redact or disable application-level diagnostics; request/response bodies can be excluded from telemetry.
- Telemetry vendors & marketplace flows: We use telemetry for service health (metrics & sampled traces). Telemetry is aggregated; no full request payloads are sent to third-party observability tools in hosted mode. AWS Marketplace listing is a commercial channel — marketplace metering events do not contain customer payloads.

Attachments: I've attached the latest redwood_subprocessors_list_v3.pdf and a short telemetry_design_notes.pdf that call out what we send (metrics, sampled spans, scrubbed logs).

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm the security contact for Acme who will own the subprocessor review?
2) Please flag any specific telemetry items (e.g., traces, full request logs) that would be a blocker for procurement.
3) If procurement needs, we can provide the SOC 2 attestation and an execution copy of the subprocessor addendum — I’ll loop in legal if needed.

Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up with your security team next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A couple of clarifying questions from our security and procurement teams before we move to the legal/contract stage:

1) Telemetry detail: when you say "no full request payloads" — can you confirm whether any sampled traces or error reports could contain PII (e.g., card last4, emails) in stack traces or request metadata? If so, can that be scrubbed automatically?

2) Retention: you mentioned 30 days by default. For audit purposes we need a firm statement of the retention windows for: (a) request/response payloads, (b) service logs, (c) metrics/metrics history. We may need 6-12 months for metrics in some regulated contexts.

3) Marketplace flow: if we procure through AWS Marketplace (for the convenience of finance), does AWS get any access to telemetry/usage details beyond metering? Specifically: will AWS be listed as a subprocessor and, if so, what data do they receive?

4) Subprocessors list: thanks for the PDF. Would you also send a spreadsheet with columns for name, purpose, country of processing, and whether the vendor has a SOC 2 or ISO cert? Procurement likes a CSV.

Procurement timeline note: if security signoff is fast we can target a July 15 PO; otherwise this may slip into August.

Subject: Re: Third-party subprocessors & telemetry (post-call follow-up) — technical answers

Hi all — quick technical answers below (happy to hop on a call if useful):

1) PII in telemetry: by default telemetry we export is metrics (counts/timings), sampled traces (span metadata), and error events. We scrub request/response bodies from traces and strip request headers that could contain PII. Stack traces are sanitized; we have a preprocessing step that redacts common PII patterns (emails, credit card numbers). We can add an automatic PII scrubbing rule for Acme if you provide any custom patterns.

2) Retention windows (hosted API default):
- request/response payloads: 0 days (not stored for analytics; ephemeral during handling unless customer opts in)
- service logs (structured logs): 30 days
- metrics/metrics time series: 365 days (aggregates only)

Note: For Dedicated / Private deployments these can be configured per contract — e.g., metrics history can be shortened or extended, logs can be shipped to customer-owned logging endpoints.

3) Telemetry vendors / AWS Marketplace:
- Telemetry vendors (we use a managed observability pipeline) do not receive full request payloads. They receive aggregated metrics and scrubbed/span-level traces.
- AWS Marketplace: AWS is listed as a commerce/entitlement provider and receives metering records required for billing. These records do not include customer payloads. We list AWS as an infrastructure/subprocessor in the marketplace context; they do not receive application-level telemetry.

4) Subprocessors CSV: attached a quick stub (I converted the current PDF list to a CSV internally). It includes name, purpose, country, cert status. I'll hand a cleaned version to Marissa for procurement.

Next steps: Marissa — I'll prepare the CSV and a short security cover note you can send to Acme. Lauren — flag if Legal wants different language on marketplace disclosures.

Thanks,
Aditya
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference

Hi John / Sara — thanks for the questions and timeline. Please see consolidated answers below (pulling from Aditya's notes) and the attached CSV.

Consolidated answers:
- Telemetry & PII: Redwood's telemetry pipeline does not include full request/response payloads. Sampled traces and error events are scrubbed for common PII patterns (emails, CC numbers) and request bodies are excluded by default. We can add custom PII patterns for Acme if you provide examples.
- Retention windows: request/response payloads: 0 days (not stored); service logs: 30 days by default; metrics: aggregates retained for 365 days. We can adjust these windows for Dedicated or Private deployments via contract.
- Marketplace / AWS: AWS Marketplace will be listed as a commerce metering provider and is included on the subprocessors list for billing/metering purposes only — AWS does not receive application payloads or unredacted telemetry.

Attachments included: redwood_subprocessors_list_v3.pdf, soc2_cert_stub.pdf, subprocessor_summary_stub.csv

1) Security contact: Sara, can you confirm whether you will own the subprocessor review or should we loop in a different person?
2) Procurement: Marissa will share the CSV for procurement; if you want an AWS Marketplace procurement flow, finance should review the metering note. Target PO date: July 15 if security signoff completes this week.
3) Security review: propose a 30-minute call this week to walk through the subprocessor list and telemetry sanitization.

If helpful, Aditya and I can provide a short cover note for procurement that summarizes the telemetry safeguards and retention guarantees for your contract.
